content.text:
The drawing shows a primary amide: a carbonyl carbon with a C=O, bonded to an N labelled "NH" at the bottom left. Since only one H is written on the N, I read this as an NH2 group with the second H left implicit. The carbonyl carbon connects to a CH2, which connects to a CH carrying two phenyl (Ph) groups.

This is 3,3-diphenylpropanamide. All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry (and the CH is not a stereocentre anyway, since it has two identical phenyl groups).

SMILES: NC(=O)CC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1
